headline: Rowand's 14th-inning single walks off the Reds
recap: Aaron Rowand's two-out single in the bottom of the 14th inning scored David Dellucci and gave the Phillies a 6-5 win over the Cincinnati Reds. Dellucci opened the inning with a single, Chase Utley walked, and Cincinnati intentionally walked Ryan Howard to load the bases before Rowand's hit ended it.

Phillies starter Jon Lieber worked seven innings, allowing three runs on five hits with seven strikeouts, with all three runs coming on a pair of Edwin Encarnacion home runs in the fourth and sixth. Reds starter Kyle Lohse held Philadelphia to one run over six and a third innings while striking out eight.

The Phillies erased a two-run deficit in the eighth on a Jimmy Rollins home run and a go-ahead RBI triple from Pat Burrell, only for Javier Valentin's pinch-hit two-run homer off Tom Gordon to put the Reds back in front in the ninth. Chris Coste's leadoff double, pinch-runner Chris Roberson, and a Shane Victorino sacrifice fly tied it again in the bottom of the ninth, and Ryan Madson, Geoff Geary and Aaron Fultz combined for five scoreless relief innings before Fultz earned the win.
